title: SoundBench: Free Online Audio Converter, Editor & Analyzer
excerpt: Free audio tools in your browser: convert FLAC, WAV, MP3 and ALAC, make ringtones, change speed and pitch, and spot fake lossless files. No uploads.
content_html:
Free audio tools, processed on your device

SoundBench is a free set of audio tools that works inside your web browser. Every file is decoded, edited and encoded on your own device with the Web Audio API, the LAME MP3 encoder and FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly. Your audio is never sent to a server.

Because nothing is uploaded, there are no file size limits beyond your device's memory, no waiting in a queue, no account and no watermark. The tools work with MP3, WAV, FLAC, ALAC, M4A/AAC, OGG Vorbis, Opus and AIFF.

What you can do with SoundBench

  • Convert audio between MP3, FLAC, WAV, ALAC, AAC, OGG, Opus and AIFF, one file or a whole album at once, with tags kept.
  • Reduce audio file size for email or messaging by picking a quality level or typing the size you need.
  • Remove or isolate vocals with AI, and split songs into vocals, drums, bass and other stems.
  • Trim audio, cut out a part, add fades and make iPhone (M4R) or Android ringtones.
  • Change volume, speed and pitch, or shape the tone with a 10-band equalizer.
  • Boost the bass, make 8D audio, reverse a song, or make slowed + reverb and nightcore edits.
  • Record your voice, remove background noise, change your voice and turn speech into text with AI that runs on your device.
  • Find the BPM and key of a song, tune an instrument and practice with a metronome.
  • Check whether a FLAC or WAV file is genuine lossless or a transcoded MP3, with a spectrogram and loudness readout.
  • Edit ID3 tags and album art, test headphones, speakers and microphones, generate test tones, and calculate file sizes and streaming data use.

Frequently asked questions

Is SoundBench free?

Yes. Every tool is free to use with no account, no daily limit and no watermark on exported files.

Are my audio files uploaded anywhere?

No. SoundBench processes audio locally in your browser. The files never leave your device, which also makes it fast for large files.

Which audio formats are supported?

SoundBench reads MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A/AAC, ALAC, OGG Vorbis, Opus, AIFF and most other common formats, and exports MP3, WAV, FLAC, ALAC, AAC, OGG, Opus, AIFF and M4R ringtones.

Does it work on phones?

Yes. SoundBench works in current versions of Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox on desktop, Android and iPhone. Very long files may need a computer because of phone memory limits.
